HR@10 against 99 sampled negatives measures ranking among 100 candidates; it does not establish full-catalog top-10 quality. Krichene and Rendle show sampled metrics can reverse model comparisons even in expectation. Fixed users and candidates improve comparability within this benchmark but do not remove sampling bias. Interpret improvements as gains under the pinned sampled protocol. [On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)

For this design, use a category-stratified paired user bootstrap: retain both models’ binary hit outcomes for each user, resample 200 users with replacement within each category using identical indices for both models, and recompute the difference between four-category macro averages. Report the observed difference and a 95% bootstrap interval. One additional hit changes category HR by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR by 0.125 points, so small differences can reflect few users. This application of [paired bootstrap resampling](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html) estimates user-sampling uncertainty conditional on fitted models and fixed candidates; it excludes training randomness, alternative negative samples, and selection effects.

Repeatedly choosing epochs and hyperparameters on the same validation users can overfit the selection criterion, making the winning validation score optimistic. A bootstrap interval computed after selection does not correct that search bias. Keep the evaluator fixed, record search breadth, treat small winning margins as provisional, and use the untouched host test only after final model selection. Independent outer evaluation or nested validation can assess the selection procedure when permitted. [Cawley and Talbot, 2010](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)
